key_insight: PIML-OFEM combines overlapping finite elements with problem-independent machine learning to reuse local basis functions across load cases and boundary conditions for large-scale heterogeneous structures.
engineering_relevance: It enables faster, high-resolution structural analysis and topology optimization while maintaining accuracy close to fine-scale finite element results.
method: Use only corner-node DOFs for each substructure.
Solve oversampled local elasticity problems on extended domains and restrict them to the target substructure.
Train a U-Net to map local Young's modulus fields to numerical basis functions, then blend bases with a partition-of-unity overlap.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with fine-scale FEM in displacement and elemental strain energy, with lower online cost than direct FEM and better accuracy than PIML substructure models using linear boundary interpolation.
watch_item: The approach still depends on a learned surrogate for local basis functions, so performance may be sensitive to training coverage across material patterns and substructure configurations.
paper_title: PIML-OFEM: A New Large-Scale Structural Analysis Method Based on Problem-Independent Machine Learning and Overlapping Finite Element Technique
